papers.title: Greater than the sum of our parts: The new division of labor in design with AI
papers.abstract: Abstract Design is how humans change the world, and in the age of AI it is increasingly a joint activity between humans and machines. This perspective argues that AI does not simply add new tools to the designer's repertoire; it has the capability to reorganize the division of labor in design and, in doing so, reshape what it means to be a designer. We distinguish between representative technologies, which model and derisk complex systems (eg digital twins, immersive simulations), and operative technologies, which act directly within design processes (eg generative and agentic systems that propose, evaluate, and select alternatives). Viewed through the Five-Cycle model of design, we argue that these technologies widen inputs, accelerate exploration, and tighten feedback across problem definition, conceptual and embodiment design, and value proposition. In our model, representative tools derisk what to believe; operative tools derisk what to try. Together these technologies could enable closed-loop, hybrid human-AI design processes in which human roles shift from manual problem solving toward stewardship, curation, translation, and, in a democratized future, even historical guardianship of designerly knowledge. We contend that design science is essential for understanding and guiding this transition: explaining how human purpose, creativity, and responsibility are redistributed in human-AI teams; developing methods to study how values propagate through automated design workflows; and informing education and practice so that increasingly automated design processes remain aligned with human intent and societal well-being.
papers.summary_ja: AIはデザイナーのツールにとどまらず、設計プロセスにおける人間と機械の分業を根本的に再編成するという視点論文。デザイン科学の枠組みを用いてAI時代のデザイン教育と実践のあり方を問い直す。

papers.title: Service innovation thinking for research infrastructure mission-oriented practices
papers.abstract: This article explores how service innovation thinking and design-informed capabilities can reposition research infrastructures (RIs) as transformative actors in mission-oriented innovation. Through applying the Future Ripples methodology, the study engages European and Latin American representatives of RIs and national innovation agencies in a structured foresight process to identify systemic levers of change. Findings indicate that embedding core service design capabilities – empathy, engagement, modelling, context sensitivity, and vision building – can help RIs transition from hierarchical, output-driven structures to participatory, user-centric platforms. Two critical transformations are highlighted: intensifying direct engagement with service beneficiaries and shifting from top-down to collaborative mission goal setting. These shifts enable more inclusive governance, greater responsiveness to societal challenges, and enhanced legitimacy of mission-driven agendas. The study contributes a practical framework for integrating design capabilities into RI operations, aligning organizational change with broader policy and socio-technical system transformations.

papers.title: A framework for assessing the social impact of design
papers.abstract: How can designers assess the social impact of their practices? The objective of the paper is to provide the foundations for the adoption of impact assessment and evaluation, especially the social one, into design practices. The paper provides an exploration of the possibilities for assessing design initiatives, the existing connections, main contributions and the potential implications for design practitioners and researchers. After a general introduction to impact assessment and evaluation, it provides an overview of what it means to assess and evaluate impact, an overview of the state of the art of Impact Assessment over the social dimension in the Design practice and research, and finally it proposes a framework for navigating, selecting, and adopting impact assessment methods and approaches in design projects. Three directions emerge: Impact Assessment for Product/Service Design, for Design for Social Innovation and for Design for Policy Making.

papers.title: Addressing service grand challenges through inductive research
papers.abstract: Purpose The paper advocates inductive methods and qualitative data for grand service challenges that are complex, uncertain and context-dependent. Revisit the inductive origins of core service concepts and show why such challenges suit induction. Offer pragmatic guidance, demonstrate how induction explicates mechanisms and builds theory (often via extreme cases and understudied actors) and outline a future agenda spanning sustainability, nonprofit and informal care, more-than-human perspectives and diverse tech- and low-tech service experiences. Design/methodology/approach This is a methodological essay and integrative review defining qualitative data and collection modes, synthesizing inductive analysis approaches and offering practical guidance for conducting inductive research. Clarifies complementarities with experiments and quantitative modelling, including abductive iteration and illustrates practices with exemplars. Findings Four insights emerge: (1) Qualitative data flexibly capture multifaceted, co-created, culturally embedded service experiences across contexts and actors. (2) Emergent inductive designs reveal unanticipated mechanisms, boundary conditions and theory – especially from extreme cases. (3) Rigorous interpretive practice leverages embodied knowledge to craft midrange, process explanations that identify causal mechanisms in context, complementing regularity-based inference. (4) Induction augments deduction by informing stimuli and measures, clarifying endogeneity and mediation and strengthening ecological validity. Inductive work forged pivotal constructs and remains vital for complex, uncertain service problems.
papers.summary_ja: 複雑・不確実なサービスのグランドチャレンジには帰納的・定性的研究が最適であることを論証し、未来の研究アジェンダを提示した統合レビュー。

papers.title: Value co-creation and co-destruction dynamics in a service system: contradictions in geocaching
papers.abstract: Purpose We propose contradiction as a theoretical lens for explaining the micro-level dynamics of value co-creation (VCC) and value co-destruction (VCD). Although these phenomena are often treated as interconnected, their exact relationship – how they dynamically interact, emerge and evolve in specific service contexts – remains insufficiently theorized and empirically examined. Design/methodology/approach We draw on data from online discussion forums and in-depth interviews with geocachers. Through interpretive content analysis, we identify disturbances such as problems, errors and conflicts. These disturbances are categorized as VCC or VCD tensions from which underlying contradictions are derived. Findings Our study shows how to uncover the dynamics of VCC and VCD in a service system. We identify eight distinct VCC and VCD practices and illustrate the associated contradictory poles embedded in the geocaching context.
papers.summary_ja: 矛盾を理論的レンズとして価値共創（VCC）と価値共破壊（VCD）のミクロダイナミクスを初めて統合実証した研究。サービスシステム管理への実践的示唆を提供。

papers.title: Assemblages of Design Activities: From Trade to Strategy
papers.abstract: There is no standard design method; every situation requires a distinct design process with a series of design activities that may change significantly. Design activities increase in number, intensity, and commitment proportionally to the ethical responsibility of the design and the complexity of the situation. Similarly, the design process is messier and less predictable. In this visual essay, I explore the potential core activities that designers may assemble when designing the design process. First, let's start with the obvious activities: sketching, prototyping, and producing. In a simple design process (e.g., an industrial designer proposing silverware packaging), designers typically perform these activities. In this instance, designing is a traditional trade. Activities focus on proposal-making, generating something that does not exist. Producing an output is the goal, or what the client has commissioned for design work.

papers.title: From energy to circularity: Examining cross-transitional learning on the Island of Ameland
papers.abstract: Island communities are widely recognized as frontrunners in sustainability transitions, often driven by cohesive social networks and a shared aspiration for self-sufficiency. This study investigates the Dutch Wadden island of Ameland, which has undergone a significant energy transition and is now pursuing both heat and circular transitions. The central focus of this research is on understanding higher-order learning—learning that transcends individual transitions and informs broader governance approaches—within and across these successive sustainability transitions. While learning is increasingly acknowledged as vital to transition success, empirical studies rarely examine how insights are transferred between different transition domains. To address this gap, we applied the learning history method, using semi-structured interviews and a focus group with local stakeholders to trace critical learning moments and their influence over time.

papers.title: Illuhmannating Technological Innovation Systems: Towards a Systems Perspective
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The Technological Innovation Systems framework operates from an economic perspective, investigating the generation, diffusion and utilization of a specific technology within a particular institutional infrastructure. Emerging from innovation sciences, the TIS framework inherited methodological individualism as the micro-level approach to explaining change. However, with the recent introduction of motors of innovation, methodological individualism has become incapable of explaining systemic change within a TIS. To take the next step in the TISs evolutionary process, we survey the theory of complex systems proposed by German sociologist Niklas Luhmann. We demonstrate how Luhmann's systems theory can account for systemic change within TISs by focusing on the communication frame of reference.
papers.summary_ja: 技術革新システム（TIS）フレームワークにルーマンの社会システム論を統合し、システミックな変化とステアリング戦略を説明できる新理論的基盤を構築した概念論文。

papers.title: Systems Thinking for T-Shaped Sustainability Education: A Viable Systems Approach (vSa)
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainability represents a complex and evolving paradigm calling for competences necessary for a deep understanding of the interdependencies among human, environmental, economic, and cultural dimensions. Along with a review of the literature and an analysis of official guidelines from leading international institutions, this study assesses key references for the competences necessary for sustainability education. Findings show that systems thinking is globally recognized as a key competence for sustainability and a core element of education programs. However, an overarching reference framework capable of enhancing coherence and synergy across global education initiatives is still lacking. To address this gap, the paper puts forward a 'T-shaped' framework, rooted in the viable systems approach (vSa), in which systems thinking can be regarded as a meta-competence within education for sustainability.
papers.summary_ja: システム思考をサステナビリティ教育のメタ・コンピテンスと位置づけ、Viable Systems Approach（vSa）を核としたT字型教育フレームワークを提案した文献レビュー論文。

papers.title: Flying high or crashing down: Pre-entry knowledge, post-entry learning, and the distribution of startup performance
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary We examine variation in high-technology startups' performance based on founders' pre-entry experiences by developing a formal model and using confidential employee-employer linked microdata from the United States to examine the empirical consistency of the model propositions. The model posits that relative to insiders, a lack of industry-specific experience creates greater epistemic uncertainty regarding optimal business models at time of entry for outsiders and thus, higher post-entry adjustment costs associated with necessary pivots. Consequently, outsiders have a higher selection threshold for the value-creation potential of the underlying technical ideas. Together, these mechanisms yield propositions that relative to insiders, outsiders have lower odds of survival on average, but higher growth and probability of being acquired.
